```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7.5,
  fig.height = 4.6,
  dpi = 120
)
library(rgraphtool)

load_or_fallback_lesmis_weighted <- function() {
  res <- tryCatch(netzschleuder_network("lesmis"), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(res) && "value" %in% graph_edge_properties(res$graph)) return(res)
  set.seed(42)
  n <- 48L
  b <- rep(1:4, each = 12L)
  el <- list()
  w <- integer(0)
  for (i in seq_len(n - 1L)) {
    for (j in (i + 1L):n) {
      same <- b[i] == b[j]
      if (stats::runif(1L) < ifelse(same, 0.35, 0.03)) {
        el[[length(el) + 1L]] <- c(i, j)
        w <- c(w, 1L + stats::rpois(1L, ifelse(same, 4.0, 0.6)))
      }
    }
  }
  g <- graph_create(n, directed = FALSE)
  graph_add_edges(g, do.call(rbind, el), properties = list(value = w))
  list(graph = g)
}
```

This article combines the `weighted_sbm` and `layered_sbm` demos, showing how
to incorporate edge weights (discrete or continuous covariates) and discrete
multiplex layers into flat and nested SBMs.

## 1. Weighted / edge-covariate SBMs

`rgraphtool` implements all five Peixoto (2018) discrete and continuous
covariate distributions (`discrete-geometric`, `discrete-poisson`,
`discrete-binomial`, `real-exponential`, `real-normal`), including simultaneous
multi-covariate models and exact change-of-variables log-Jacobians via
`transform_weights()` for comparing raw vs. log-transformed continuous models.

```{r weighted-sbm, fig.height = 4.5}
lesmis <- load_or_fallback_lesmis_weighted()
g <- lesmis$graph

w <- graph_edge_property(g, "value")
summary(w)

# Discrete count covariate models (MAP description length)
set.seed(42)
cmp_disc <- compare_weight_models(
  g,
  weights = "value",
  nested = TRUE,
  method = "map",
  nruns = 3L
)
print(cmp_disc)

# Continuous and log-transformed weight models with exact Jacobian adjustment
set.seed(42)
cmp_cont <- compare_weight_models(
  g,
  weights = "value",
  candidates = c("real-exponential", "real-normal", "log-normal"),
  nested = TRUE,
  method = "posterior",
  nsamples = 80L,
  thin = 5L,
  burnin = 40L
)
print(cmp_cont)

best_w <- cmp_disc$best_state
set.seed(42)
unw <- minimize_nested_blockmodel_dl(g)
ov_w <- partition_overlap(nested_levels(best_w)[[1L]], nested_levels(unw)[[1L]],
                          norm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("Level-0 partition overlap (weighted %s vs unweighted): %.3f\n",
            cmp_disc$best_model, ov_w))

old_par <- graphics::par(mfrow = c(1L, 2L), mar = c(7, 4, 3, 1))
tab <- cmp_cont$summary
graphics::barplot(
  tab$delta,
  names.arg = tab$model,
  las = 2,
  ylab = "Delta(-log P(A, w)) [nats]",
  col = ifelse(tab$model == cmp_cont$best_model, "darkorange", "steelblue"),
  main = "Continuous weight models (0 = best)"
)
graphics::par(mar = c(2, 2, 3, 1))
plot_hierarchy(best_w,
               main = sprintf("Weighted nested SBM (%s)", cmp_disc$best_model))
graphics::par(old_par)
```

## 2. Layered (multiplex) SBMs

When discrete edge types stratify a network into layers, `compare_layered_models()`
compares the **edge-covariate** hypothesis (`independent = FALSE`, where layers
are edge labels on a shared topology) against the **conditionally independent
layers** hypothesis (`independent = TRUE`, where each layer is generated
independently given the shared vertex partition).

```{r layered-sbm, fig.height = 4.6}
cat(sprintf("N = %d vertices, E = %d edges, C = %d discrete layers\n",
            graph_num_vertices(g), graph_num_edges(g), length(unique(w))))

set.seed(42)
cmp_l_map <- compare_layered_models(
  g,
  layers = "value",
  models = c("edge_covariates_dc", "edge_covariates_ndc",
             "independent_layers_dc", "independent_layers_ndc"),
  nested = TRUE,
  method = "map",
  nruns = 3L
)
print(cmp_l_map)

set.seed(42)
cmp_l_post <- compare_layered_models(
  g,
  layers = "value",
  models = c("edge_covariates", "independent_layers"),
  nested = TRUE,
  method = "posterior",
  nsamples = 80L,
  thin = 5L,
  burnin = 40L
)
print(cmp_l_post)

best_l <- cmp_l_post$best_state
old_par <- graphics::par(mfrow = c(1L, 2L), mar = c(9, 4, 3, 1))
tab_l <- cmp_l_map$summary
graphics::barplot(
  tab_l$delta,
  names.arg = tab_l$model,
  las = 2,
  ylab = "Delta(DL) [nats]",
  col = ifelse(tab_l$model == cmp_l_map$best_model, "darkorange", "steelblue"),
  main = "Layered model variants (0 = best)"
)
graphics::par(mar = c(2, 2, 3, 1))
plot_hierarchy(best_l,
               main = sprintf("Layered SBM (%s)", cmp_l_post$best_model))
graphics::par(old_par)
```
